segments.text: Something that drives me crazy is that
people just underestimate, massively
underestimate the communication gap
between them and the agents. When you're
asking the agent to do stuff, right, it
is like a colleague or someone you're
employing to do something for you, to
build some code for you.
And just like when you work with an
employee, there is a communication
barrier between you and the agent. And
the thing about that barrier is it's not
going to go away as models get better.
The model is never going to know exactly
what you're thinking. And so, you're
always going to have to improve and get
over that communication barrier. That's
because it's not a model problem, it is
a human problem. We often don't know
what we want. We have complicated
internal value systems for the things
that we want to prioritize in the output
that we're getting from the agent. And
crucially, the agent doesn't know what
we care about. We care about complicated
things in complicated orders. And
communicating that to an agent is really
hard cuz we often don't know it
ourselves. So, when you want to get
better outputs from your agent, then
think about that communication barrier.
Keep it always in mind. And think, what
does the agent not know about me? Or
what does it not know about what I want
right now?
